verification.verification_note: The full article was recovered from Tampere University. It surveys 91 municipalities in Germany, Norway and Finland about determinants of organisational AI capability.

admission.reason: Although European and empirical, the study concerns municipal organisational AI adoption rather than the European research-and-innovation system.

metadata_correction.reason: Institutional and publisher metadata list the final journal publication in 2022; 2021 is the early-online year.

results.reader_what: The study models organisational factors associated with AI capability across 91 European municipalities.
results.reader_why: Public-sector adoption is not itself an R&I-system mechanism.
results.reader_more: Using an extended technology-organisation-environment model and structural-equation analysis, the paper identifies financial costs, innovativeness, government pressure, incentives and regulatory support as significant determinants. Its unit of analysis is municipal administration.

deep_analysis.research_question: What factors enable European municipalities to develop organisational AI capabilities?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Five organisational/environmental factors are associated with municipal AI capability formation, while citizen pressure and perceived value are not significant.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Survey of technology managers in 91 municipalities across Germany, Norway and Finland, analyzed with structural equation modelling.
deep_analysis.qualification: The evidence is rigorous but addresses government-agency technology adoption rather than European R&I funding, talent, research infrastructure or research governance.
